messages:
Jordan S.: customer on private VPC seeing intermittent 502s / TLS handshake resets during streaming inference. ticket #7892. root cause unclear, attaching tcpdump snippet.

Jordan S.: ```
# tcpdump -nn -r capture.pcap 'tcp and (port 443 or port 53)'
10:12:01.123 IP client -> nat 443: SYN
10:12:01.223 IP nat -> client 443: SYN, ACK
10:12:01.224 IP client -> nat 443: ACK
10:12:03.500 IP client -> nat 443: PSH, ACK
10:12:03.502 IP nat -> client RST
```

Andre (CSE): customer says it happens on larger responses (>1MB) and only from their private VPC. they use NAT Gateway + custom NACLs.

Sasha N.: probable NACL or SG issue. NACLs are stateless — you must allow both directions for ephemeral ranges. common misconfig: deny ephemeral ports inbound which causes RSTs on larger transfers when return uses high ports.

Sasha N.: recommended NACL sample:
```
# NACL (stateless) order matters
100 ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0
110 ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0
* DENY ALL
```

Priya R.: also check DNS egress/return (UDP 53) and conntrack on the NAT appliance. repro steps i gave to customer:
1) tcpdump on their NAT: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/cap.pcap 'tcp or udp port 53'`
2) reproduce with: `curl -v --http2 https://api.redwood.example/private/stream -H "x-stream-test:1"`
3) `ss -tanp | grep :443` and `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` (if using NAT instance)

Jordan S.: temporary workaround suggested: add NACL allow for TCP 1024-65535 both in/out and allow UDP 53 both in/out. customer applied change, monitoring.

Andre (CSE): if it doesn't resolve, we'll ask for full pcap and NAT config (is it an appliance?). if they're on an appliance NAT with port preservation it could reuse ephemeral ports leading to RSTs; recommend test against AWS NAT Gateway or assign dedicated EIPs.
